quick.summary: How to change a live application without throwing your users offline.
quick.takeaway: Build the new version next to the old one, then switch the traffic.

beats.line: My server upgrade broke the application for hours. Can we stop this?
Think of a bridge. You never rebuild it while cars drive over it.
You build a second bridge next to it.
Exactly. Build the new server beside the old one.
Then route the users to the new setup.
What if the new one breaks?
You route users back to the old one instantly.
The industry calls this a blue green deployment.
Can I just call it a parallel swap?
That is much clearer. Parallel swap.
So I build the new version entirely, then flip the switch?
Yes. Your users will not notice a thing.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of a parallel swap?
options: It is cheaper than replacing old servers
You can switch traffic safely and instantly
It automatically writes code for you
quiz.explanation: Because the new server is already built, you can switch traffic instantly and roll back just as fast.

quiz.question: During a parallel swap, you destroy the old environment before building the new one.
quiz.explanation: You build the new environment next to the old one, keeping both running until the switch is successful.
